suite.name: AOT/C++: complete dasProfile 16 workloads and maintained 8 workloads
notes: Only AOT and C++ measured. Builds, regression tests and corpus validation finished before timing. Benchmark processes ran sequentially.
Original Vela workload source, sizes, C++ adapter input values and compiler flags are unchanged. The C++ sort adapter now uses std::stable_sort instead of std::sort.

Vela sorting still preserves rooted snapshots, callback mutations, exceptions and stable original-position tie breaking. The benchmark comparator has no side effects; callback contracts are tested separately.

Maintained immediate integer results no longer register a redundant RootRange in the benchmark harness. Future results remain rooted while pumping. Nanosecond arithmetic changes include this measurement correction and cannot all be attributed to compiler optimization.

The old binary remeasurement retains its original unstable C++ sort lane, which is historical context only. AOT speedups compare the same stable Vela sort workload; current AOT/C++ ratios use the corrected stable C++ baseline.
Prior limitations for integer widths, managed/native object layouts and normal allocation remain. The maintained spectral norm uses double and int64 indices on both sides.
The C++ calls microbenchmark explicitly keeps PlainStep noinline; its ratio is specific to that workload and is not a public C++ facade timing.

1583 C++ tests passed; 112 Python tests passed and 2 platform distribution tests skipped. The linked native fixture includes 49 GoogleTests. 85 existing programs matched VM/AOT values, output, exit status and errors; 3 invalid programs were rejected by both. No lint was run.

findings: canPlace body_9 has only a cold leaf_failure call; successful paths have no root registration or resource-frame calls. Overflow and bounds branches remain.
sort entry_15 has no call_indirect relocations; the comparator and structural-version checks are inlined into its comparison loop.
tree merge/split use roots_enter/exit for borrowed stack roots and retain write barriers for non-null references. The object has no set_global or generic equality helper imports.

comparison_to_previous.reason: C++ sort now uses stable_sort and maintained immediate-result timing excludes redundant harness rooting. Other original kernels, machine and timing options match; focused AOT old/new remeasurements are retained.

suite.name: Unified AOT/C++: 8 maintained and 16 ported dasProfile workloads
notes: All workloads use the existing benchmarks target, vela_aot_benchmarks executable and --aot-compare report.
Only AOT and C++ were selected for full timing. All 64 registry cases, including the existing VM and first-native cases, passed a separate one-iteration smoke run.
Compilation, preparation, instantiation and warm-up are excluded; normal allocation, GC and checksum verification remain timed.
Ported workloads use double floating-point arithmetic, deterministic inputs and stable sorting. SHA and iterative Fibonacci wrap explicitly at 32 bits.
Refactored C++ storage and validation, and the merged executable, differ from the historical temporary experiment; these ratios are not a direct compiler regression comparison.
Process resident counters share one process and include previous workloads; they are neither standalone AOT footprint nor peak RSS.

comparison_to_previous.reason: The benchmark inputs are now checked in and use one executable and one harness; C++ storage and validation differ from the temporary experiment.
